The [link functions](#def-link-function) listed in the structure of a [GLM](#def-glm) are not all on the same footing.
For each outcome distribution, the form of its density singles out one link.
To say which, we need the density's *natural parameter*.

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#def-natural-parameter}
#### Exponential dispersion family, natural parameter, and canonical link

A distribution belongs to the **exponential dispersion family**
if its [density](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pdf) (or [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf)) can be written as

$$
f(y; \theta, \phi)
= \expf{\frac{y\,\theta - b(\theta)}{\phi} + c(y, \phi)}
$$

for some functions $b(\cdot)$ and $c(\cdot, \cdot)$.
The parameter $\theta$ is the **natural parameter**,
and $\phi > 0$ is the **dispersion parameter**.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{Y} &= b'(\theta) \eqdef \mu \\
\Varf{Y} &= \phi\, b''(\theta) = \phi\, V(\mu),
\end{aligned}
$$

where $V(\mu) \eqdef b''(\theta)$,
written as a function of $\mu$,
is the **variance function**.
The **canonical link** is the link function $g(\cdot)$
that sets the [linear predictor](#def-linear-predictor) equal to the natural parameter:
$g(\mu) \eqdef \theta$
[@dobson4e, Chapter 3; @dunn2018generalized, Chapter 5].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-canonical-link-numeric}
#### Natural parameters of a Poisson and a Bernoulli outcome

For a [Poisson](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-poisson) outcome with mean $\mu$,

$$
f(y; \mu)
= \frac{\mu^y e^{-\mu}}{y!}
= \expf{y \logf{\mu} - \mu - \logf{y!}},
$$

so $\theta \eqdef \logf{\mu}$, $b(\theta) \eqdef e^\theta$, and $\phi \eqdef 1$.
For a [Bernoulli](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-bernoulli) outcome with success probability $\pi$,

$$
f(y; \pi)
= \pi^y (1 - \pi)^{1 - y}
= \expf{y \logf{\frac{\pi}{1 - \pi}} + \logf{1 - \pi}},
$$

so $\theta \eqdef \logit(\pi)$, $b(\theta) \eqdef \logf{1 + e^\theta}$, and $\phi \eqdef 1$.

The code below checks both forms against R's built-in densities,
at $\mu = 3$, $y = 2$ and at $\pi = 0.25$, $y = 1$,
and computes $b'(\theta)$ and $b''(\theta)$ for the Bernoulli case.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
mu <- 3
theta_pois <- log(mu)
y_pois <- 2
pois_exp_form <- exp(y_pois * theta_pois - exp(theta_pois) - lgamma(y_pois + 1))
pois_check <- isTRUE(all.equal(pois_exp_form, dpois(y_pois, mu)))

pi_bern <- 0.25
theta_bern <- qlogis(pi_bern)
y_bern <- 1
bern_exp_form <- exp(y_bern * theta_bern - log1p(exp(theta_bern)))
bern_check <- isTRUE(all.equal(bern_exp_form, dbinom(y_bern, 1, pi_bern)))

b1_bern <- plogis(theta_bern)
b2_bern <- b1_bern * (1 - b1_bern)
```

- For the Poisson distribution with $\mu = 3$,
  the natural parameter is $\theta = \log(3) =$ `r round(theta_pois, 4)`,
  and the exponential-family form gives
  $f(2) =$ `r round(pois_exp_form, 4)`,
  which matches `dpois(2, 3)`: `r pois_check`.
  Here $b'(\theta) = b''(\theta) = e^\theta =$ `r round(exp(theta_pois), 4)`,
  so $V(\mu) = \mu$.

- For the Bernoulli distribution with $\pi = 0.25$,
  the natural parameter is $\theta = \logit(0.25) =$ `r round(theta_bern, 4)`,
  and the exponential-family form gives
  $f(1) =$ `r round(bern_exp_form, 4)`,
  which matches `dbinom(1, 1, 0.25)`: `r bern_check`.
  Here $b'(\theta) = \expit(\theta) =$ `r round(b1_bern, 4)`,
  which is $\pi$,
  and $b''(\theta) = \pi (1 - \pi) =$ `r round(b2_bern, 4)`,
  so $V(\pi) = \pi(1 - \pi)$.

Consequently, the canonical link for the Poisson distribution is the log link,
and the canonical link for the Bernoulli distribution is the logit link.
:::
